What it requires: Give individuals notice before processing their personal data, and be transparent about its purpose and use.
References: Australia APPs 1 and 5 · CPRA 1798.100(a), 1798.130 · PIPEDA Sch 1, Principles 2, 3 and 8 · Colorado 6-1-1308(1) · GDPR Art 12 · NZ IPP 3 · Singapore PDPA ss 12(d), 20

What it requires: Have a legal basis for processing personal data: consent, performance of a contract, vital interests, public interest or other legitimate interests.
References: PIPEDA Sch 1, Principle 4.3 (consent) · GDPR Art 6 · NZ IPPs 10 and 11 (after collection) · Singapore PDPA s 13 (consent)

What it requires: Collect personal data only for specified, legitimate purposes in line with the Privacy Policy, and don't process it in ways incompatible with them.
References: Australia APP 6 · CPRA 1798.100(c) · PIPEDA Sch 1, Principle 4 · Colorado 6-1-1308(2), (4) · GDPR Art 5(1)(b) · NZ IPP 10 · Singapore PDPA ss 18, 20

What it requires: Collect only personal data that is relevant and necessary for the stated purposes, and keep it only as long as needed.
References: Australia APP 3.1–3.2 · CPRA 1798.100(c), 1798.100(a)(3) · PIPEDA Sch 1, Principle 4 · Colorado 6-1-1308(3) · GDPR Art 5(1)(c) · NZ IPPs 1 and 9 (storage limitation) · Singapore PDPA s 14(2)(a)

What it requires: Apply technical and organisational measures that protect personal data, limit access to authorised personnel and take reasonable steps to prevent breaches.
References: Australia APP 11 · CPRA 1798.100(e), 1798.150(a) · PIPEDA Sch 1, Principle 7 · Colorado 6-1-1308(5) · GDPR Art 32 · NZ IPP 5 · Singapore PDPA s 24

What it requires: Consider privacy throughout the design and operation of services and systems: limit collection to what is needed, secure the data and respect individuals' rights.
Meet the requirements and restrictions that apply to processing by processors and service providers.
References: CPRA 1798.100(d), 1798.140(ag)(1) · Colorado 6-1-1305 · GDPR Art 28 · NZ IPP 5, s 11 · Singapore PDPA s 4(2)

What it requires: Don't discriminate through processing: people can refuse or withdraw consent and keep using the services where that is possible, and automated processing must not discriminate.
Keep records of processing: relationships with controllers and sub-processors, the purposes and categories of processing, disclosures, and other records that show compliance.
References: Australia APP Guidelines 1.5 · PIPEDA s 10.3 · GDPR Art 30 · Singapore PDPA s 22A

What it requires: Carry out data protection impact assessments to understand and mitigate the risks of processing to individuals' rights and freedoms.
References: Australia Privacy Act s 33D, APP Guidelines 1.7 · CPRA 1798.185(a)(15) · Colorado 6-1-1309 · GDPR Art 35

What it requires: Notify supervisory authorities and affected individuals of personal data breaches.
References: Australia Privacy Act Part IIIC · PIPEDA ss 10.1–10.3 · GDPR Arts 33 and 34 · NZ Privacy Act Part 6, Subpart 1 · Singapore PDPA ss 26A–26E

What it requires: Register or communicate privacy program details with supervisory authorities where required, and appoint a Data Protection Officer accountable for implementing, monitoring and reporting on privacy obligations.
References: Registration: GDPR Art 37(7) · Singapore PDPA s 11(5). Data Protection Officer: Australian Government Agencies Privacy Code · PIPEDA Sch 1, Principle 1 · GDPR Art 37 · NZ Privacy Act s 201 · Singapore PDPA s 11

What it requires: Follow the requirements and restrictions on transferring personal data internationally.
References: Australia APP 8 · GDPR Arts 44–50 · NZ IPP 12, Part 8 · Singapore PDPA s 26
